verdict.rationale: Unleash's own Environments feature gives each stage (development, test, production) a separate flag configuration, so you can enable and test a flag outside production. Backend tokens are scoped to a single environment, which keeps SDK and automation access isolated. However, environments separate flag configuration, not data. Nothing documents a true sandbox instance or tenant where an AI agent (via the Admin API or MCP server) can safely run mutations against isolated non-production data. missing for 10: documented sandbox/test instance with data isolation from production, guidance for agents/API/MCP to target a non-production environment, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: each environment has different feature flag configurations. This allows you to enable a flag in development or test without enabling it in production.
Environments represent different stages in your development lifecycle. They allow you to manage your product releases from local development to production.
Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
